items: Choose a firearm that shares the same licence section (Section 13/15/16).
Only one firearm from the same licence section (Section 13/15/16) can be added to a renewal.
Select the competency certificate you want to use for this application.
You can only add one competency certificate to a renewal application.
If only one competency certificate is available for your profile, the app may select it automatically.
A valid form of proof of identity.
Accepted documents must be clear, in colour where possible, and show the same full names used on the application.
The following are accepted forms of identity:
South African ID card (photos of front and back);
Green barcoded ID book (photo of photo/ID number page);
Valid passport (photo page with photo, passport number, expiry);
For foreign nationals: Passport and permanent residence permit.
Document must show your residential address and your name, dated within the last 3 months at the time of submission.
Examples of proof of address include (this is not a complete list):
Municipality/water/electricity bill;
Bank letter or stamped statement with address;
Lease/rental agreement signed by both parties.
Select the firearm you want to include for this application.
You can only add one firearm licence to a renewal application.
If only one firearm has been added to your profile, the app may select it automatically.
For Section 518(a) renewals, firearm choices are filtered by the categories on the selected competency certificates.
If a firearm does not match any selected competency category, it will not be available for selection.
GunCerts shows two competency certificate expiry calculations so you can compare them side by side.

Cert issue date expiry: This starts from the competency certificate issue date. If matching firearms are Section 13 only, the app uses 5 years. If any matching firearm is Section 15 or 16, the app uses 10 years.
Firearm-based expiry: This uses the soonest valid expiry date from firearms that match at least one category on the competency certificate.
Reminder styling uses the earliest valid expiry date across the available calculations so the app takes the more cautious view.
The certificate card shows the issue date together with both calculated expiry values.
Different DFOs may calculate competency expiry differently. This setting lets you choose which approach your DFO uses so reminders and card highlighting follow the same method.
Comp issue date: Uses the competency certificate issue date. If matching firearms are Section 13 only, the app uses 5 years. If any matching firearm is Section 15 or 16, the app uses 10 years.
Firearm expiry: Uses the earliest valid firearm expiry date from firearms that match at least one category on the competency certificate.
I don't know: Keeps the more cautious approach and shows a warning when the two methods lead to different reminder outcomes. This is the safest approach.
Changing this setting resets competency reminders so they can be recalculated using the selected method.
Add your firearm storage to the application. This should show the safes where the firearms of the application will be stored.
If possible also include proof that the safes are SABS 953-1 or 953-2 compliant and properly mounted to a fixed structure.
You can upload an installation certificate, invoice, or clear photos that prove compliance and mounting.
If you use more than one safe, upload evidence for each.
You can add additional safes by pressing the "+" button.
For each safe, upload at least the following photo evidence:
The safe with the door closed (show entire safe);
The safe with the door open (empty it for your safety);
The bolts used to secure the safe to the wall/ground/other fixed surface.
The built-in GunCerts character reference wizard is the easiest way to get your personalised character references for firearm licence applications.
Once you have created the character references, they will automatically be added to your application.
You don't have to use this wizard if you prefer to use your own character references.
Provide written statements from people who know you well and can confirm you are responsible and of sound mind to possess a firearm.
Statements should be signed and dated by the nominated individuals.
Not all DFOs require character references for competency renewals. We recommend that you check with your local DFO to confirm if they require this.
Suggested person for the 1st statement: spouse/partner or a family member.
Suggested person for the 2nd statement: a friend, neighbour or colleague.
Suggested person for the 3rd statement: another friend, neighbour or colleague.
You can choose one of three options: create a motivation using the wizard, use the standard motivation text, or indicate that you will attach your own motivation.
The motivation wizard uses your selected application firearm and profile data to generate a structured motivation letter for your application.
If you choose standard motivation text, GunCerts includes the following wording for each firearm attached to the renewal application:
"I declare that the circumstances for the use of this firearm have not changed, and that it is still used as originally motivated."
"I confirm that I have continued to comply with all the requirements under which the firearm was originally licensed to me."
"Since the licence was issued, I have adhered to all stipulations and regulations of the Firearms Control Act (FCA) and will continue to do so."
Use the wizard option when you want a generated motivation, use the standard text option for the built-in wording, or select your own motivation if you prefer to submit your own motivation.
Check with your local DFO what they expect for renewal motivations before submission.
The application form provides detailed guidance of the passport photo requirements.
Submit two recent colour passport-size photos with a plain background.
Write your full name and ID/passport number on the back of each photo before handing them in at the station.
For Section 16 firearms, you require proof of up-to-date firearm association membership and dedicated status certificate(s).
Some associations issue both a membership card and a separate letter confirming your current membership. Others issue only the letter.
If you are a member of more than one firearm association, include all relevant memberships.
You can add additional memberships by pressing the "+" button.
Upload the letter from your association that confirms your current membership or good standing.
For most associations, this is the main document that proves you are currently a paid-up member.
The letter should show your name and the association name.
If available, it should also show your membership number and current membership validity.
Some associations issue this letter on its own, while others issue it together with a separate membership card.
Proficiency documents are generally not required because your competency certificate usually covers this requirement.
Some Designated Firearms Officers (DFOs) may still ask for proficiency documents to be included with the application.
If you are not sure whether to include them, check with your local DFO before you submit.
Only include proficiency documents that are relevant to the application you are creating.
Make sure the document clearly shows the training provider and the firearm type covered.
If you upload proficiency documents, they will be included in the checklist and supporting documents bundle for the application.
Certificate or letter from your association confirming your dedicated hunter status.
Ensure the certificate covers the period when you submit the application.
Certificate or letter from your association confirming your dedicated sport shooter status.
Validity dates must extend beyond the application submission.
You are confirming you have not been convicted of an offence under the Firearms Control Act that resulted in imprisonment without an option of a fine.
If you have any convictions or pending matters, disclose them to your Designated Firearms Officer with supporting documents or an affidavit.
You confirm you have not been declared unfit to possess a firearm in terms of the Firearms Control Act.
If you were previously declared unfit but the status was lifted, submit proof of the upliftment with your application.
You undertake to carry the firearm in accordance with Section 98(5)(a) of the Act and Regulation 78.
Use a proper holster or safe container, keep the firearm under your control, and do not leave it unattended in vehicles or public places.
You confirm you have a safe that is securely mounted to a fixed structure and complies with SABS 953-1 or 953-2.
If renting or in a shared property, ensure the mounting is permitted and that only you have access to the keys or combination.
Upload your firearm association membership documents.
When adding your firearm association membership, you'll need:
Proof of your valid and current membership from your firearm association.
Membership card if your association provides one.
Dedicated status certificate(s) (Hunting and/or Sport shooting).
If your association issues endorsements, you will be able to add them here for each firearm you've added to the app.
A phone with a camera, a good quality image, or a single page PDF of the relevant documents.
Some associations issue only a letter that confirms your current membership. Others issue both a letter and a separate membership card. Add both if your association provides them.
Tips for a clear photo
Clean your camera lens to reduce image blur and glare.
Place the documents on a plain, solid-colour background.
Keep the photo in focus so details are sharp and readable.
Hold the camera steady and fill the frame with the document.
Use good lighting and avoid glare or heavy shadows across the text.

For your safety, make sure the safe is empty and accessible.
Wipe dust or glare off the plates and serials.

GunCerts shows two competency certificate expiry calculations so you can compare them side by side.

Cert issue date expiry: This starts from the competency certificate issue date. If matching firearms are Section 13 only, the app uses 5 years. If any matching firearm is Section 15 or 16, the app uses 10 years.
Firearm-based expiry: This uses the soonest valid expiry date from firearms that match at least one category on the competency certificate.
You can set the calculation method used by your DFO in the Settings tab under Preferences. The default setting applies both methods and notifies you of the soonest expiry date.
When adding a competency certificate, you'll need:
Your SAPS competency certificate and good lighting.
A phone with a camera to take a photo of your certificate.
You can also upload an existing photo of your competency certificate from your photo library.
Tips for a clear photo
Clean your camera lens to reduce image blur and glare.
Use good lighting and avoid glare or heavy shadows across the text.
Place the certificate on a plain, solid-colour background.
Keep the photo in focus so details are sharp and readable.
Hold the camera steady and fill the frame with the certificate page.
We will guide you through photographing the front and back of your licence card and scan the barcode to prefill the firearm details.
Before you start
Have your SAPS firearm licence card ready.
A plain, solid-colour background to put your card on.
Remove anything that could be obstructing the barcode, like stickers or dirt.
Make sure you can photograph/upload images of the FRONT and BACK of the card.
NOTE: some older firearm licence barcodes will not scan. Input firearm info manually in these instances.
Tips for a clear photo
Clean your camera lens to reduce image blur and glare.
Place the licence card on a plain, solid-colour background.
Keep the photo in focus so details are sharp and readable.
Hold the camera steady and fill the frame with the licence card.
Use good lighting and avoid glare or reflections on the card.
